posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
Tony was worried that his table and recording system wasn't stable enough for a three minute exposure. He did it anyway and just reported that it worked! 8) I can just see him totally Zen'd out ... sitting in a dark room, trays all full of meticulously mixed chemical baths, watching a clock, listening intently for low frequency noises that might excite a component, waiting for just the right moment to open The Shutter of Commitment. 

We all know how many tiny little things can mess up a hologram recording. I'm just amazed that it works at all! It's the time from just before I open that shutter to its closing I like best about the practice of holography, though. It's theatrical, scientific, and a gamble. It's de-stressing and spiritual. 

I like the little necessity of taking a break for the settling time. I like the focus on background vibrations in a quiet moment. I like the paranoia that comes about a third of the way into the exposure, about helicopters and motorcycles comming by. 

I was just wondering what it is about holography that motivates those who practice it. What's your hook?

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md:
My hook?

I'm addicted to holography! The holography bug bit me.

Just as a redneck lets his kids go bareboot but can come up with enough money to buy a new shotgun; I'll find some way to buy a new laser or some holography film even if the house roof needs new shingles or the car needs tires.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **BobH:** I like the little necessity of taking a break for the settling time. I like the focus on background vibrations in a quiet moment. I like the paranoia that comes about a third of the way into the exposure, about helicopters and motorcycles coming by.

(Well said !!!)

Or toilets flushing, doors slamming, dogs barking, all the stuff you don't normally notice. Her Majesty stomping about upstairs. It occurs to me 

that lasers are cheap enough that I could just set up a separate interferometer near the table just to let me know if I really did have a vibration problem during the exposure and then I could develop the plate with suitably diminished expectations.

I do like that quiet moment....

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **BobH:** I was just wondering what it is about holography that motivates those who practice it. What's your hook?

It's that time when the hologram is drying and the image is starting to appear like magic. At that point I'm completely drawn in and could just stare at the things, continuously examining all the details while turning the hologram about in the light.
